title: Privacy for Linear Circuits
statement: Let $F$ be a field, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $B$ be a finite set of nonzero field elements with $|B|<k$. For any two assignments of field elements to the input indices, there is a bijection of the families of input polynomials of degree less than $k-1$ such that, for every family $q$ of such polynomials, every party in $B$, and every linear circuit $C$, BGW evaluation on the first assignment using $q$ gives that party the same value as evaluation on the second assignment using the image of $q$ under the bijection.
hypotheses_covered: The set $B$ has cardinality strictly less than $k$
Both input assignments are arbitrary functions from input indices to $F$
